source_contract.statement: Reject subscription creation before every mutation when the current user cannot read skill metadata.
Published and yanked subscriber fanout use current visibility and access facts before recipient dispatch.
VisibilityChecker is the only visibility decision source; fact resolvers must not introduce a parallel model.
English and Chinese denial messages plus private, namespace-only, hidden, removed-member and disabled-user tests are required on subscribe and fanout paths.
PRIVATE metadata access retains owner or namespace ADMIN/OWNER behavior while the absent SubscriptionMetadataAccessPolicy class is not reintroduced.
Stale subscription rows must be filtered at current-read time from /me/subscriptions, including response total, without deleting rows.
SubscriptionMetadataAccessPolicy is absent from base and candidate r3 and therefore cannot be an existing base interface to preserve.
evidence: PR #735 head e071afb4 contains the class

source_contract.statement: VisibilityChecker has eight production call sites whose observable behavior must remain compatible.
A full-context VisibilityChecker overload centralizes account, namespace, membership, platform-role and narrow access-purpose semantics while old overloads remain unchanged.
NotificationService.create requires a new physical transaction so AFTER_COMMIT CallerRuns persists before SSE.
The denial code resolves to the frozen English and Chinese copy in plan-r1.
Unsubscribe remains a revocation escape and isSubscribed remains an own-row boolean because neither response exposes metadata.
No migration, prune, historical row cleanup or subscription count repair is included.
No confirmPublish, event producer or event record change is included because #738 is already in base.
No workflow file, public PR branch or publication state is modified in the engineering plan.

invariants.statement: Subscription mutation occurs only after current metadata read access succeeds.
PRIVATE remains readable to the owner or current namespace ADMIN/OWNER and denied to ordinary members across every new path.
Missing or non-active accounts reach no metadata mutation, response or recipient sink, even with role bindings.
Denied subscribe performs zero row, count and event effects; allowed non-idempotent subscribe performs all once.
Loss of current metadata access does not prevent deletion of the caller's retained subscription row.
Unsubscribe decrements exactly once only when an own row exists.
isSubscribed preserves authenticated own-row boolean and anonymous false behavior without metadata.
Retained rows whose skills are missing or no longer readable expose no SkillSummaryResponse fields.
The /me/subscriptions total and items both describe the current-readable set and do not reveal stale row count.
Filtering /me/subscriptions performs no delete, counter decrement or migration side effect.
source_evidence: HD-32 no prune or cleanup boundary

invariants.statement: Fanout uses account, membership and RBAC facts loaded at event handling time rather than subscription-time state.
Fanout and retained-row page filtering use bounded batch authority reads and no per-candidate repository lookup in their decision loops.
Authority source failure occurs before every recipient row, SSE and metadata response sink.
Published fanout skips publisher and yanked fanout skips actor after eligibility without affecting other recipients.
A genuine yank may bypass only the latest-null guard; private, hidden, membership, account, namespace and actor gates remain enforced.
Subscriber eligibility, notification failure or shared-executor saturation does not suppress, duplicate or reorder the independent published search-index consumer.
Rolled-back or no-transaction event publication produces no registered AFTER_COMMIT subscriber or search sink.
Eight existing VisibilityChecker call sites and old overload matrix remain observably identical.
No SubscriptionMetadataAccessPolicy class or resolver-local visibility decision tree is introduced.
Current account, membership and platform-role facts determine subscribe, retained-row reads and fanout.
Only eligible, de-duplicated recipients reach durable row, SSE and later list payload sinks.
A notification row commits before matching SSE; SSE failure does not undo the row.
IN_APP preference is evaluated only after authorization and cannot cause an ineligible recipient to pass.
With executor capacity, the registered listener runs only after source commit and produces committed row before SSE.
A saturated running configured executor may run on publisher thread but still commits row before SSE.
Reflection, generated, external and runtime-conditional paths remain explicit audit residuals rather than absence claims.
